body.statement: If \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), every selector gate is laid back on \(E_H\), and \(S\) has no latent root shared with \(V\), then \(G_H^N\) is the ordinary semi-Markovian expansion on \(V\), \(\Phi_H\) equals its ordinary observational-target relation, and \(\operatorname{SA\mbox{-}CS\mbox{-}ID}\) reduces to the ID formula-or-hedge classification of Shpitser and Pearl.
body.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check that the new calculus agrees with classical completeness when systematic selection disappears.
body.gap: Classical ID supplies the known endpoint, while the new work must show that the support-aware state and certificate semantics collapse to it exactly.
body.consumer: Implementers can regression-test the new backend against established ID outputs on ordinary hidden-variable DAGs.
body.proof_tex:
Exact support \(H=\{s_\emptyset\}\) implies \(P(S=s_\emptyset)=1\).  Since every gate is laid back at that value, the known multiplexer selects the natural structural equation at each substantive node.  The absence of a latent root shared by \(S\) and \(V\) ensures that suppressing the now deterministic selector coordinate does not remove a substantive common cause.  The retained normalization deletes only the constant gate arguments and keeps every natural response table and latent-root law.  Consequently its substantive recursive equations are precisely those of the ordinary semi-Markovian expansion on \(V\).

For every \(v\),
\[
p_\theta(V=v,S=s_\emptyset)=p_\theta(V=v),
\]
and intervention at \(S=s_\emptyset\) changes no laid-back gate.  Normalization equivalence therefore identifies \(\Phi_H\), after omission of the constant selector coordinate, with the ordinary pair consisting of the observational law of \(V\) and the intervention \(do(A=a)\) target.

There is no active selector override, so \(\Sigma\) is empty and selector correction is vacuous.  The reachability predicate in \(\textnormal{def:fixing-transition}\) is the ordinary CADMG predicate \(\operatorname{dis}_D(W)\cap\operatorname{de}_D(W)=\{W\}\), and its kernel quotient is the ordinary fixing quotient.  The two cases in \(\textnormal{def:elimination-transition}\) are ordinary marginalization and proper-district factorization.  Hence every admitted nonresidual transition agrees algebraically with its ordinary counterpart.  Nothing in these observations forces the finite residual lists \(\mathcal P\) and \(\mathcal C\) to contain a standard hedge certificate, so the stronger classification claim does not follow.
